chapter_theme: The one song at Vayiravivanam (வயிரவிவனம்) on the Saraswati river: a plea for the jnana to bow at the feet of those who keep Murugan's feet in mind, with Murugan as the guru who told Brahma the first word.

655.reading: The poet asks Murugan to grant him the jnana to bow at the feet of those who think daily in their hearts of his flower feet. The praise names him son of the Mother who dwells with Hara, whose toes crushed the hero who lifted the mountain, nephew of Rama who bridged the sea, six-faced and twelve-armed in the sun's light, the jnana guru who told Brahma, the speaker of the Vedas, to say the first word within his own speech, the vel that freed the gods, at Vayiravivanam on the Saraswati amid fragrant groves and blue-lily pools.
655.nuance: The plea is twice removed: not for the feet, but to bow at the feet of those who hold his feet in mind (கருத்தர் தாள்கள் பணிய), service of devotees as the form of jnana. சுருதிகள் உரைத்த வேதன் உரைமொழி தனக்குள் ஆதி சொலு: the challenge to Brahma to speak the first word is the Om episode, but Om is not named.

links.note: 655 asks for the jnana to bow at the feet of those who hold Murugan's feet in mind (நினைவுறு கருத்தர் தாள்கள் பணியவும்). Tirumular calls the ash-wearing devotees gods walking on earth (அடியார் நிகழ் தேவர்கள்) and says those who honour them as the Lord himself have no karma. Both put the devotee in the Lord's place as the object of worship.
